4. The bath during active controls can be bounded directly

I did not replace active-window bath evolution by an independently postulated circuit-noise model.

For a one-site Pauli coupling, group all its Bohr frequencies:
$\mathcal L_{iP}(\rho)
=
\sum_\omega\gamma_\omega
 P Q_\omega\rho Q_\omega P
-\frac12\{G,\rho\},
\qquad
G=\sum_\omega\gamma_\omega Q_\omega.$
The $Q_\omega$ are orthogonal local projectors summing to the identity. Hence
$\boxed{\|\mathcal L_{iP}\|_\diamond\le2\gamma_{\max}.} \tag{7}$
There is no multiplicative penalty from the number of Bohr frequencies.

If each stabilizer has weight at most $w$ and each qubit belongs to at most $q$ checks, a coupling is supported within a neighborhood of size
$h_0\le1+q(w-1),$
and the local sum of generator norms is at most $6h_0\gamma_{\max}$.

During a strict bounded-depth layer of local controls, conjugation enlarges supports only by a fixed amount. The coherent drift can be canceled using the allowed bounded control $-H$, while retaining the original Davies dissipator. Imperfections in that control are still charged.

A Trotter expansion, with CPTP resummation of unmarked factors, then gives a local-norm fault envelope
$q_{\mathrm{bath}}=2\theta^{1/L}, \qquad \theta\le1, \tag{8}$
where $\theta$ is the integrated incident bath-generator norm and $L$ is a computable overlap constant.

This is a bound on sums of fault-path superoperators. It does not assume that Davies faults are independent stochastic Paulis, or that they have a freely supplied Poisson-fault representation.

Equation (8) supplies a positive size-independent small-rate interval for an active construction that has an appropriate local-norm threshold. It does not supply the missing passive retention theorem, nor a complete joint threshold for every primitive, terminal measurement and resource preparation in this processor.
